# Beryllium: Feature Matrix

<!-- Generated by freebsd/tools/feature-matrix from plan/feature-matrix.toml. Do not edit by hand. -->

Status as of 2026-11-04, latest release v0.20.3.1-1. Every feature the project must implement, build and test, with where it is specified, the code that does it, and the test that proves it. Edit `plan/feature-matrix.toml` and run `freebsd/tools/feature-matrix`; CI rejects a row that claims a test, code or source the repository does not have.

## Legend

| Column | Values |
|---|---|
| Priority | **must**: needed for the first release (plan/09); **should**: wanted for it; **later**: after it; **study**: decide first |
| Phase | roadmap phase (plan/09): 0 baseline, 1 native build, 2 Capsicum renderer, 3 other processes, 4 jail and resources, 5 MAC study, 6 release engineering |
| Implemented | **done**; **partial**; **todo**; **inherited**: Chromium or Helium code Beryllium keeps as it is; **disabled**: present but off in Beryllium (the row says why) |
| Built | the release whose package contains it, or **no** |
| Tested | **passing** / **failing**: the test's latest recorded run on FreeBSD (Evidence names the build, machine and date); **manual**: checked by hand (Evidence); **written**: the test exists, with no passing run recorded on the current release; **planned**: the plan names a test, not written yet; **none**: no test planned |

## Browser functionality

What a user does with the browser on FreeBSD. Evidence "owner, 0.20.3.1" means the maintainer's machine: FreeBSD 16.0-CURRENT, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 Laptop (driver 595.99.02), KDE Plasma on Wayland. "15.1 package" runs were made on the same machine on 3 November 2026, before the release; the browser suite has not yet been rerun in full on the release.

| `F-GPU-01` | **GPU acceleration and WebGL.** Compositing, rasterisation and WebGL are hardware accelerated where the driver allows. | should | 1 | **inherited** | v0.20.3.1-1 | **passing**<br>`freebsd/tests/browser/tests/test_40_rendering.py::test_webgl_webgpu_canvas`<br>`freebsd/tests/browser/tests/test_40_rendering.py::test_gpu_info`<br>owner, 0.20.3.1 on NVIDIA, suite run 4 Nov 2026; Intel and AMD untested; owner, 0.20.3.10, 7 Nov 2026: passing without the lockdown; with it the default canvas read back 18,52,87 for #123456 (86 expected, as in 0.20.3.8 with the lockdown), WebGL fine; owner, 0.20.3.11, 8 Nov 2026: three rendering runs (lockdown off, on, 2D canvas forced to software) all read 86 on the default and on a CPU canvas, so the 87 looked like a one-off GPU readback; owner, 0.20.3.12, 8 Nov 2026, lockdown on: both the default and the CPU canvas read 18,53,86, so it is not the GPU and happens only under the lockdown (2 of 5 lockdown runs, 0 of 7 default runs); the test is exact on both canvases again and records a colour sweep (plan/14 increment 4); the same day, lockdown on, both canvases read 18,52,87 again: three of six lockdown runs off by one, zero of eight default runs; owner, 0.20.3.13, 9 Nov 2026: the grey sweep found one in four sampled greys one level off in one channel on the CPU canvas, with and without the lockdown (+1 throughout one run, -1 throughout the other, channel varying); #123456 and the default canvas exact in both; WebGL fine, WebGPU no adapter; 9 Nov 2026, six more 0.20.3.13 runs: the moved greys of each run share one residue modulo 4 with a per-run seed, which is Helium's canvas fingerprinting noise (P-FPR-04), not a rendering fault; the rendering test now runs with the noise off and awaits its first run; owner, 0.20.3.14, 10 Nov 2026, six runs with the noise off: every sweep exact on both canvases, by fill and by putImageData, WebGL fine; owner, 0.20.3.16, 10 Nov 2026, the first runs with the Intel GPU driver loaded beside NVIDIA's (Intel on the laptop panel, NVIDIA on the external display): with --render-node-override=/dev/dri/renderD128 the GPU process renders on NVIDIA and the rendering and media groups pass; with renderD129 it reports ANGLE on Mesa 26.2.2, Intel Graphics (ARL), and the browser process ends about a second after every start (21 errors and 2 failures of 38 tests, all a closed DevTools connection), cause unknown: the suite did not say how the process ended and does from this date; a second pair of runs the same day gave the same two results; from Chromium's source, the browser renders on the compositor's main device unless the switch names another, and ends on any Wayland error, so a compositor that cannot show the other GPU's buffers is a candidate cause, unconfirmed until the log of such a run or a start without the switch is seen; confirmed the same evening from that run's log and the kernel's: Mesa's Intel driver declined every buffer layout the compositor offered (Unsupported modifier, three times), the compositor refused the buffer sent instead (libwayland error 7, importing the supplied dmabufs failed), and each browser exited on signal 5, Chromium's stop on a Wayland error; the pairing is unsupported by the desktop, not a fault in the browser, and the documentation of the switch says what it requires; two lockdown runs the same evening without the switch: the browser chose renderD128 by itself and rendered on the NVIDIA GPU, everything in the rendering and media groups passing | plan/01-PROJECT-CHARTER.md D6<br>plan/08-TESTING-AND-VERIFICATION.md §2.4 |

## Privacy

What Beryllium promises about the network and the user's data, and the privacy features it inherits from Helium and ungoogled-chromium.

a second run on the NVIDIA node the same day: both origins moved 1031 pixels, the fourth set, which the model had given before any report showed it, and exactly the model's set for token low bits 0 (three of eight comparisons with a shared set); a lockdown run with the new suite the same evening: both origins moved set 1 (998 pixels), and test_moved_pixels_depend_on_the_whole_token named it, as it will on every build before 0.20.3.17 (four of nine comparisons) | README.md |

## Security

The sandbox and hardening work, Beryllium's reason to exist. Nothing in this area confines a process yet: the release ships with no sandbox, and says so.

### Capsicum renderer sandbox

| ID | Feature | Priority | Phase | Implemented | Built | Tested | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `S-REN-01` | **Renderers in capability mode.** Every production renderer enters Capsicum capability mode before it handles web content, and the browser checks it with the kernel. *Opt-in. Not yet a sandbox: in 0.20.3.3 renderers inherited directories (/, /usr...) and writable profile files, gone in 0.20.3.4 (S-IPC-01); they still hold shared memory as writable unlinked files in /tmp, replaced by sealed memfds with limited rights in 0.20.3.5 (S-SHM-01, S-SHM-02); 0.20.3.7 hands renderers no swap file, so they hold no writable file. Still missing: the allowlist, least rights on every descriptor, the kernel check, default on. From 7 Nov 2026 the sandbox tests are a gate when the lockdown is requested: a renderer not in capability mode, or unreadable, fails them instead of being skipped (plan/16 BER-04). From 0.20.3.13 the lockdown logs the thread count at its point (RendererMain locks down before RenderThreadImpl exists) and the gate requires 1. The threads=-1 of 0.20.3.13 and 0.20.3.14 was the lockdown discarding the count it had read (the sweep's result replaced the whole Confinement); kept from 0.20.3.15.* | must | 2 | **partial**<br>`patches/security/beryllium-capsicum-renderer.patch`<br>`patches/security/beryllium-renderer-tracing-after-lockdown.patch`<br>`patches/platform/beryllium-bsd-kernel-thread-names.patch` | no | **manual**<br>`freebsd/tests/browser/tests/test_50_sandbox.py::test_capability_mode_per_process`<br>`freebsd/tests/browser/tests/test_50_sandbox.py::test_threads_at_the_lockdown_point`<br>`freebsd/tools/tests/test_sandbox_gate.py`<br>`freebsd/tools/tests/test_thread_dump.py`<br>owner, 0.20.3.3 with --enable-features=BerylliumCapsicumRenderer, 4 Nov 2026: every renderer in capability mode (procstat), the whole suite passes; trap mode stops renderers at their first refused call (cpuset_getaffinity); owner, 0.20.3.4, 5 Nov 2026: the same, and no inherited directory or profile file left; owner, 0.20.3.6, 5 Nov 2026: every renderer in capability mode, the suite passes apart from the descriptor test (one unnamed file per renderer); owner, 0.20.3.7, 5 Nov 2026: every renderer in capability mode and the whole suite passes; owner, 0.20.3.8, 7 Nov 2026: the same with per-descriptor rights, but renderers spun on a kqueue poll (fixed for 0.20.3.9); owner, 0.20.3.10, 7 Nov 2026: every renderer the browser listed in capability mode, idle CPU 0.00 s; the gate caught one renderer the browser had just launched and not yet at its lockdown point, so the tests now give a listed renderer five seconds to get there; owner, 0.20.3.11, 8 Nov 2026: every listed renderer in capability mode, the lockdown log clean, the gate passing apart from the policy test (two renderer-made sockets, S-REN-05); owner, 0.20.3.12, 8 Nov 2026: every listed renderer in capability mode, the lockdown log clean, the two socket pairs cut at creation (made on CrRendererMain and Compositor); ### Shared memory and descriptors

| ID | Feature | Priority | Phase | Implemented | Built | Tested | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `S-SHM-01` | **Anonymous shared memory.** Shared memory is created with memfd_create and seals (SHM_ANON as fallback), never in a named namespace. *Until 0.20.3.4 every region was an unlinked file in TMPDIR (the Linux memfd path was Linux-only), so renderers held writable files and page content reached a disk file system. From 0.20.3.5: memfd_create, sealed against shrinking and growing, no file fallback. The oracle (mem.memfd_seal, mem.shm_named) shows memfd with seals works in capability mode and named objects do not, on 14.5, 15.1 and 16.0.* | must | 2 | **done**<br>`patches/security/beryllium-anonymous-shared-memory.patch` | no | **passing**<br>`freebsd/tests/browser/tests/test_50_sandbox.py::test_renderer_shared_memory_is_anonymous_and_limited`<br>`freebsd/tests/browser/tests/test_50_sandbox.py::test_renderers_hold_no_directories_or_writable_files`<br>owner, 0.20.3.6, 5 Nov 2026, with and without the lockdown: renderers hold their shared memory as memfd objects (test_renderer_shared_memory_is_anonymous_and_limited passes) and the whole suite passes otherwise; one unnamed writable file per renderer remains, not from PlatformSharedMemoryRegion (S-REN-06) | plan/06-SECURITY-MODEL.md §3.3<br>plan/03-ARCHITECTURE.md §4.4<br>plan/10-RISKS-AND-OPEN-QUESTIONS.md R6 |
| `S-SHM-02` | **Read-only memory stays read-only.** The browser limits a shared-memory descriptor's rights before passing it, so a renderer cannot map a read-only region writable. *The read-only twin is a dup limited to CAP_MMAP_R, CAP_FSTAT and CAP_FCNTL (F_GETFL only); the writable descriptor to CAP_MMAP_RW, CAP_FSTAT and CAP_FCNTL; Chromium's access-mode check reads the rights. The oracle (mem.ro_twin_map_rw, _mprotect, _map_exec, _introspect) shows on 14.5, 15.1 and 16.0 that the twin cannot be mapped writable or executable or upgraded with mprotect. The suite test checks the rights of every shared memory descriptor in renderers.* | must | 2 | **done**<br>`patches/security/beryllium-anonymous-shared-memory.patch` | no | **passing**<br>`freebsd/tests/browser/tests/test_50_sandbox.py::test_renderer_shared_memory_is_anonymous_and_limited`<br>owner, 0.20.3.6, 5 Nov 2026: procstat -C in renderers shows writable regions with read, write, seek, mmap read-write, fstat and fcntl only, read-only twins with read, seek, mmap read-only, fstat and fcntl; no ftruncate or executable mapping anywhere | plan/06-SECURITY-MODEL.md §3.3<br>plan/12-WORK-PLAN-AND-RED-TEAM.md §10 |

No LD_PRELOAD interceptor exists.* | must | 2 | **inherited** | no | **passing**<br>`freebsd/tests/browser/tests/test_45_fonts.py::test_same_platform_fonts_with_and_without_lockdown`<br>owner, 0.20.3.8, 7 Nov 2026: test_45_fonts passes, the same platform fonts (Liberation Serif, DejaVu Sans, FreeSans, FreeSerif, Noto Color Emoji) for nine scripts in a confined renderer as in an unconfined one | plan/03-ARCHITECTURE.md §4.3<br>plan/03-ARCHITECTURE.md §4.5 |
| `S-SHM-04` | **No shared socket directories.** Display and audio sockets are connected before lockdown; no confined process holds a directory where other programs' sockets live. | must | 2 | **todo** | no | **planned**<br>sandbox suite: no reach to shared socket directories; a renderer cannot connect to the X11 or Wayland socket | plan/03-ARCHITECTURE.md §4.3<br>RT-06<br>plan/10-RISKS-AND-OPEN-QUESTIONS.md R15 |

### Launcher and IPC

| ID | Feature | Priority | Phase | Implemented | Built | Tested | Source |

Fixed in 0.20.3.4 with close() and closefrom(2) between fork and exec. Rights limits on what the launcher passes: only shared memory so far (S-SHM-02, 0.20.3.5); from 0.20.3.9 the receiving renderer cuts the rest itself (beryllium-descriptor-rights.patch), which is not a boundary; from 0.20.3.13 the browser cuts every descriptor it sends a renderer launched with the lockdown on, before sendmsg (beryllium-sender-side-rights.patch: the launcher registers the pid as a confined peer, Mojo's transport cuts by kind; a writable File System Access handle keeps a writable kind).
